senses.gloss: m. du. (or שְׁחָלִים pl.) (answering to λεπίδιον, cmp. שְׁחוֹלִית) a kind of cress or pepperwort (Lepidium sativum, v. Löw Pfl., p. 396).
units: <cite ref="Gittin 57a:12">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite> <he>כפר שיחליים … מן שחליים</he> the place was called K’far Shiḥlayim, because their support came from the traffic in cress; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5:16">Y. Taan. IV, 69ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>כפר שיחליא דהוון מרביין בניהון כאילין תחלוסייא</he> (not <he>ביניהון</he>) it was named K’far Shiḥlaya, because they reared their children as carefully as cress is cultivated; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:1">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite> (Matt. K., reading <he>באילין</he>, they reared their children on cress-dishes).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 30b:2">Ab. Zar. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>השחלים</he> (Rashi <he>השחליים</he>) cress-dish (chopped cress mixed with wine or oil).

Ib. 67ᵃ וכך היו עושין … וקורין אותן שיחליים (Ar. קדירת שחלים) and so they used to prepare it at Sepphoris on Fridays, and they called it cress-dish; Y. ib. V, 44ᵈ top וקורין אותו שחלייא; a. e.—כפר שחליים (כפר שחלייא) pr. n. pl. K’far Shihlayim (Shiḥlaya), a town in the mountains of Ephraim (King’s Mountain); v. supra.
